title: I HAVE DELIVERED IT INTO YOUR HANDS

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then the Lord said to Joshua, "See, I have delivered Jericho into your hands, along with its king and its fighting men. March around the city once with all the armed men. Do this for six days. Have seven priests carry trumpets of rams' horns in front of the ark. On the seventh day, march around the city seven times, with the priests blowing the trumpets. When you hear them sound a long blast on the trumpets, have the whole army give a loud shout; then the wall of the city will collapse and the army will go up, everyone straight in." — Josh 6:2-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before a single soldier moves, God speaks in the past tense: "I have delivered Jericho into your hands." Not "I will," but "I have." In God's eyes the victory was already won. Israel's job was not to achieve the victory but to walk in obedience toward a victory God had already granted. What a difference that makes to how we face our battles.

Then God gives the strangest battle plan in history. March around the city. Blow trumpets. On the seventh day, march seven times and shout. No battering rams, no siege towers, no clever military strategy — just marching and shouting. By every human standard, this plan was foolish.

But that was exactly the point. God chose a method that made it impossible for Israel to take any credit. When the walls fell, no one could say, "Look what our army did." Everyone would know it was God alone. God often works in ways that look weak or foolish to us, so that the glory clearly belongs to Him.

This is the pattern of the gospel itself. God saves us through what the world calls foolish — a crucified Saviour — "for the foolishness of God is wiser than human wisdom" (1 Cor 1:25). Our part is not to be impressive but to obey. The victory has already been won by Christ; we simply walk in it by faith.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you approach your battles as already-won in God, or as depending on you?
2. Are you willing to obey God even when His way looks "foolish" by worldly standards?
3. How does it free you to know God works so that the glory clearly belongs to Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that the victory is already Yours. Give me faith to obey Your way, even when it looks foolish, so that You receive all the glory. Amen.
